records.topic: 2022 CRF250R/RX: bar holder positions (handbook)
records.statement: Honda's 2022 CRF250R/RX handbook: the lower bar holders are offset 5 mm from their centre line, so turning them 180 degrees sets the bar 10 mm behind standard, and the top bridge has an optional pair of holes 26 mm ahead of the standard ones, giving four bar positions in all.

source.name: Honda 2022 CRF250R/CRF250RX Owner's Manual & Competition Handbook (62K95X10), European edition

records.topic: 2022 CRF250R/RX: clutch, brake lever and pedal adjustment (handbook)
records.statement: Honda's 2022 CRF250R/RX handbook: clutch lever free play is 10-20 mm measured at the lever end; front brake lever position is set by turning the lever adjuster; brake pedal height is set by turning the rear master cylinder push rod within its standard length of 78.6-80.6 mm and locking it.

source.name: Honda 2022 CRF250R/CRF250RX Owner's Manual & Competition Handbook (62K95X10), European edition

records.topic: Renthal 839 Fatbar: the Honda CRF bend (dimensions)
records.statement: Renthal lists its 839 Fatbar as the bend for Honda CRF from 2018 (and Kawasaki KX from 2021): 802 mm wide, 91 mm high, 51 mm rise, 51 mm sweep, 131 mm clamping width, 200 mm control length, 28.6 mm clamp diameter. Renthal says Honda moved to this bend from its 2019 models.

source.name: Renthal, 839 Fatbar product page and 2021 bend recommendations

records.notes: Bar maker data. Renthal calls 839 the Honda CRF 2018+ bend; Honda does not publish its stock bar dimensions, so treat it as the matching aftermarket bend, not a Honda spec.

records.topic: KX450: ERGO-FIT four bar positions and two footpeg positions
records.statement: Kawasaki's KX450 page lists ERGO-FIT adjustable parts: four handlebar positions and two footpeg positions, to suit body size and preference, with medium-compound ODI lock-on grips.

source.name: Kawasaki (Latin America) KX450 model page

records.notes: The page covers the current KX450 and lists 2023-2024 models; no millimetre figures given. Footpeg lowering amount (5 mm) is in record kx-092.

records.topic: TF: rider-fit adjustments (owner's handbook)
records.statement: Triumph's handbook: bar height is set by rotating the bar in its clamp; the bar leaves the factory in the rear position and turning the lower clamps 180 degrees moves it 9 mm forward; front brake and clutch levers have span adjusters for hand size; brake pedal height is set with an adjuster screw, then the push rod is set for free play at the pedal; the shift pedal sits by an alignment mark on the shaft and can be moved a spline up or down.

source.name: Triumph Owner's Handbook TF250-X and TF450RC Edition (3850529-US-EN issue 1)

records.topic: 2020 CRF250R/CRF250RX: bar positions, levers and pedal (handbook)
records.statement: Honda's 2020 CRF250R/CRF250RX Owner's Manual & Competition Handbook: the lower bar holders are offset 5 mm from their centre line and the top bridge has an optional pair of holes 26 mm ahead of the standard ones, giving four bar positions: 26 mm forward, 16 mm forward, standard and 10 mm back; the front brake lever reach is set with an adjuster and lock nut; clutch lever free play is 10-20 mm at the lever end (cable clutch); the rear brake pedal should sit about level with the right footpeg, set by turning the master-cylinder push rod; Honda's personal-fit page also says to set the levers so they work comfortably seated and standing, set the shift and brake pedals close to the boot without being pressed when sitting or standing, leave the lever clamps just loose enough (or on Teflon tape) to rotate in a fall, and that bar width can be trimmed equally from both ends, a little at a time, for shoulder width.

values.brake_pedal_height: about level with the right footpeg

source.name: Honda 2020 CRF250R/CRF250RX Owner's Manual & Competition Handbook (US)

records.notes: The 16 mm position is the forward holes with the holders turned (26 - 10); Honda prints it in the 2020 and 2021 position charts.

records.topic: 2020 KX450: adjustable ergonomics (owner's manual)
records.statement: Kawasaki's owner's manual (Adjustable Ergonomics): to suit different riding positions the handlebar holders can be fitted in the alternative holes and turned around 180 degrees (near and far positions, four in all), and the right and left footpegs can each be mounted in one of two positions; the front brake lever position is adjustable. The manual gives no millimetre figures for the positions.

source.name: Kawasaki 2020 KX450 (KX450J) Owner's Manual (part 99803-0044, KTIVS public manual portal)

records.notes: Position count from the manual figure (two holder positions x two directions) and Kawasaki ERGO-FIT pages; millimetre steps for some years are in the Kawasaki 2021 KX250 press kit (record kx-092): 25 and 15 mm forward, stock and 10 mm back; footpegs 5 mm lower in the second position.
